chapter: Hampton, Andy Kirk and Charlie Barnet
title: Facing the Army induction board
summary: Called up while with Barnet at the Capitol Theatre, he tells the draft psychiatrist he would not fight and is rejected.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah, '41, '42, it was pretty rough. Like, we were at here the Capitol Theatre, I think at one time, and they called me up for the induction meeting to the Army and shit, and I told them, "I ain't fighting for nobody. Are you kidding me? I must be crazy." But they told me, "Well, either you fight or you go to jail." So I said, "Well, I ain't going to jail and I ain't gonna fight. Now, what are you going to do about that." So the cat said, "Send him in and let him talk to the psychiatrist." So I went in to the psychiatrist, and I said, "Well, man, why should I fight? I ain't mad at nobody over there. I wouldn't know the difference between a White guy or a colored guy." I said, "If he's White, I'm gonna shoot him, whether he's a Frenchman, a German... How the fuck would I know the difference?" So he said, "Well, we can't use you."
Had you had trouble with your eye at that time?
Oh, yeah, I had had trouble with my eye.
Well, they wouldn't have taken you on that, would they?
Yeah. They didn't give a shit.

Taking everybody. They was tough. But I told them, I said, "Shit, I don't know. I'll shoot any son of a bitch that's White that comes up in front of me." And they said, "No, we can't use you." And I was working with Charlie Barnet at the time.

No, he didn't know I was working with Charlie Barnet. So I mean, I wasn't ready to go dodge no bullets for nobody, I'll tell you that. I really wasn't for that, you know. And I like America, but I didn't like it that much! I mean, it's all right to be a second-class citizen, but shit, to be shot at, that's another damn story, you know. No, I couldn't make that.
